title: Clopen derived scalar comparison and its normalized compositor
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a finite set, and $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes covering $X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Work on their small pro-etale sites in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, $R_i=R|_{X_i}$, and let $r_i$, $G$ and $e_i$ be the restriction, sectionwise product gluing, and zero insertion functors of [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

Use unbounded derived module categories and localization functors $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheaf scalar tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], flat-term K-flat complexes [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex], and derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every coefficient ring sheaf $B$, let $r^B_{D,i}:D(B)\to D(B|_{X_i})$ be the degreewise restriction functor specified in [lem-pur-clopen-unbounded-derived-localization].

For every morphism $a:R\to S$ of commutative ring sheaves, with $S_i=S|_{X_i}$, there is an $S_i$-linear natural isomorphism
$$d_{a,i,K}:r^S_{D,i}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S)\xrightarrow{\sim}r^R_{D,i}K\otimes_{R_i}^{\mathbf L}S_i.$$
It is natural on all derived objects and morphisms and independent of resolution choices. On every flat-term K-flat $R$-complex $P$, it is the localization of the $S_i$-linear chain isomorphism $r_i(P\otimes_RS)\cong r_iP\otimes_{R_i}S_i$, $p\otimes s\mapsto r_ip\otimes r_is$, under canonical K-flat computation comparisons. Termwise $P\otimes_RS$ is K-flat with flat terms over $S$, and its restriction has the same properties over $S_i$.

For composable maps $R\xrightarrow{a}S\xrightarrow{\psi}T$, put $T_i=T|_{X_i}$, and let $\gamma_K:(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S)\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}T\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}T$ be the canonical scalar compositor of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization], with component version $\gamma_{i,K}$. The following two maps from $r^T_{D,i}((K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S)\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}T)$ to $r^R_{D,i}K\otimes_{R_i}^{\mathbf L}T_i$ are equal:
$$d_{\psi a,i,K}\circ r^T_{D,i}(\gamma_K)
=\gamma_{i,r^R_{D,i}K}\circ(d_{a,i,K}\otimes_{S_i}^{\mathbf L}1)\circ d_{\psi,i,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S}.$$
On $P$ both paths send $(p\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $r_ip\otimes\psi_i(r_is)r_it$. For the identity coefficient map $d$ agrees with the unit identifications, represented by $r_ip\otimes u\mapsto u\,r_ip$.

No flatness of the ring maps is assumed. The comparisons apply in particular to the finite quotient coefficient maps and the projections from the completed coefficient sheaf of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], under the coefficient identifications of the gluing node, preserving quotient transitions and their composition. Empty components, empty partitions and zero coefficient sheaves are allowed.
